_note: Every sound in the game (§6 of MILESTONES: sixteen sounds, three music layers). Sound EFFECTS are synthesised in the browser from the specs below; MUSIC is generated offline by Lyria and shipped as files. See _whyNote.
_whyNote: Gemini has Lyria 3 for music and TTS for speech, and NO dedicated sound-effects model — checked against the API docs, not assumed. Prompting a music model for a 90ms shotgun report gets you a short piece of music about a shotgun. So effects are synthesised: oscillators, noise and envelopes through Web Audio. That is also the better answer for this game. It matches the architecture already here (a hand-written PNG codec rather than sharp, an atlas built from a manifest), it adds no dependency and no download, every sound is a few numbers you can tune in this file, and retro synthesis is stylistically right for pixel art in a way a recorded sample is not.
_specNote: wave: sine|square|saw|triangle|noise. freq/freqTo sweep over the sound's life. decay is seconds. Sounds are polyphonic and rate-limited per key so sixty hits in a frame do not stack into a wall — see limitPerSecond.

master._muteNote: Both persist to localStorage under rdf.audio so a muted player stays muted.

shootLight._note: Scattergun, Sidearm, Nail Gun. Short and dry; it fires constantly, so anything with a tail becomes a drone.

shootHeavy._note: Varmint Rifle, Grenade Launcher, Drum Gun.

swing._note: Pitchfork and Sledge. A whoosh, not an impact — the impact is a separate sound and they must not merge.

crit._note: Deliberately brighter and a fifth up from `hit`, so a crit is audible in a crowd without being louder.

playerHurt._note: Never rate-limited below the i-frame cadence: missing the sound that tells you you are dying is the one unacceptable drop.

mine._note: The pickaxe tick. Quiet and frequent — it is a texture that tells you the tool is working, not an event.

bossTell._note: The Bull pawing the ground. Low, rising, and long enough to react to — §9 wants every attack telegraphed.

music._note: Three layers (§6). Generated offline by `npm run music` with Lyria 3 and committed to public/audio as mp3 — a music model is the right tool for music, and generating it at runtime would be a network call in a game loop. Layers cross-fade rather than cut.
music._promptNote: These prompts are the source of truth for the soundtrack. Re-running the tool regenerates from them; tune the prose, not the audio.

field._when: Waves 1-11. The farm is still a farm.
field.prompt: Sparse, unhurried instrumental Americana. Fingerpicked acoustic guitar and a lonely pedal steel over a slow brushed snare. Warm, rural, slightly melancholy, like an empty field at dusk. No vocals. Loopable, steady tempo around 84 BPM, no dramatic build.

combat._when: Waves 12-24, and any wave with heavy pressure.
combat.prompt: Driving instrumental country-rock with menace. Palm-muted electric guitar riff, insistent kick and tambourine, low fiddle drone underneath. Rural horror, not action-movie heroics. No vocals. Loopable, around 128 BPM, relentless rather than building.

boss.prompt: Heavy, slow, dread-filled instrumental. Detuned baritone guitar, groaning cello, sparse thunderous drum hits with lots of space between them. The sound of something very large and very patient. No vocals. Loopable, around 70 BPM, oppressive.
